gen-fs-nippo-manrope: Manrope keeps its curves wide open and its line steady. Nippo sits over it with tall little letters that look cut from wire, giving the page a technical edge.
gen-fs-nippo-satoshi: Nippo's lowercase stands nearly as tall as its capitals, every stroke looking snipped from bent wire. Satoshi follows with a soaring x-height and a plain sans finish.
gen-righteous-fs-nunito: Fat, fun, rod-bent letters fill every line of Righteous with swagger. Nunito then rounds things off with soft terminals and big lowercase bowls, so its size can stay modest beside the loud heading.
gen-tourney-fs-pilcrow-rounded: Tourney stretches wide, bulky and cut at one width, like lettering on a team jersey. Pilcrow Rounded is its warm, tight-set counterpart.
gen-fs-chubbo-gf-labrada: Labrada reads as bookish and dignified, its small letters opening wide on the page. Chubbo, with its marker-tip looseness and smooth bends, makes that formality feel casual and inviting.
gen-syne-gf-domine: Domine reads as refined and dignified, with a slight pinch where its curves meet the stems. Syne, its crossbars as fat as its stems, gives that old-world poise an experimental, commanding edge.
gen-gf-gugi-fs-alpino: Distinctive and bold, Gugi lifts its tall lowercase almost to cap height, each curve matching its stems exactly. Alpino brings a cozy, casual sans with tight spacing.
gen-gf-tektur-fs-familjen-grotesk: Familjen Grotesk reads as lively and neutral, with bowls left open on one side and a tall lowercase. Tektur, built from pipe-cleaner strokes with outsized small letters, feels far more expressive beside it.
gen-gf-wallpoet-fs-hind: Stencil-cut and loud, Wallpoet is a skeleton outline where paper shows between its letters, set at one fixed stroke. Hind is the quiet counterweight, steady as a drawn string.
gen-fs-quilon-archivo: Tall and confident, Quilon swells and thins in a gentle ebb and flow, with large open counters. It handles headlines; Archivo handles text with outward-opening curves.
